the durability of adhesives is a complex issue and that there is no single method to assess it.
all adhesive systems have a certain durability, and that the durability of a particular adhesive is a function of its clinical application procedure and the type of substrate.

, in the long term, all adhesive approaches are susceptible to failure.
the current adhesives are durable, and their clinical application is not a major problem as long as they are applied properly.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the current in vitro test protocols are capable of predicting clinical performance of adhesives in terms of durability, and that the three step adhesives remain superior in this regard.
the clinical performance of contemporary adhesions is quite good and that the durability of adhesion is mainly a function of the adhesive chemistry.
